correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the quantum cut-rank criterion from graph-state amplitudes, the exact conditional laws for overlapping and disjoint pairs, event-pair multiplicities, and the isolated-vertex covariance. Conditional full-rank probabilities reduce to uniform F2 row comparisons; symbolic expansion yields the stated positive covariances and n-dependent variance. Mean-square isolation identity follows from exact E[D Z] and Var Z; every limit holds as n tends to infinity. Exhaustive exact-rational enumeration of 64, 1024, and 32768 labeled graphs and direct partial traces in 264 sample graphs confirm finite cases, without treating them as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A random graph state is 2-uniform exactly when all its two-site marginals are maximally mixed; the count of successful pairs is a natural graded entanglement-resource statistic. Its variance cannot be recovered from marginal success probability alone. The result gives two structurally distinct strictly positive pair covariances for all n>=4, an exact full count variance, and a non-obvious rare-isolate fluctuation mechanism (the isolate effect controls leading variance but only one third of mean failures). This provides a concrete, interpretable benchmark for graph-state randomness and 2-uniformity, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
